requirements.text: The system shall retain learner progress data (completed lessons/modules) while the learner is actively enrolled in a course.
requirements.rationale: Progress tracking implies data retention at least until the course is completed or the learner unenrolls.

requirements.text: As a learner, I want the platform to require authentication (e.g., login with email and password) before accessing courses or progress data, so that my learning data is private and secure.
requirements.rationale: The transcript implies a learner-focused system with personal progress tracking, which necessitates access control to protect user data, though authentication was never explicitly discussed.

requirements.text: The system shall store learner progress data (e.g., completed lessons) securely and ensure it is only accessible to the learner, so that personal information remains confidential.
requirements.rationale: The system tracks individual progress (c0, c8), which is personal data requiring protection under privacy principles, even though the stakeholder did not mention security.

requirements.text: The platform must comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding collection, storage, and processing of learner personal data.
requirements.rationale: Any system handling personal data like learning progress must adhere to legal frameworks, a standard regulatory requirement not addressed in the conversation.

requirements.text: As a learner, I want the system to provide a mechanism to delete my account and associated data upon request, so that I can exercise my right to erasure.
requirements.rationale: Data privacy regulations typically require user data deletion capabilities, which is implied by the personal nature of progress tracking but never mentioned.

requirements.text: As a learner, I want courses to be organized by difficulty level, so that I can select courses appropriate to my current skill level.
requirements.rationale: The interviewer proposes difficulty-level grouping as an alternative, and the learner's failure to reject this option in the residue indicates it may be a valid requirement not captured in the existing user stories.

requirements.text: The platform shall not require complex progress tracking metrics (e.g., quiz scores, time spent, certificates), so that the interface remains simple and focused on learning.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 states they do not care about specific tracking metrics and just want to focus on actual learning.

requirements.text: As a learner, I want the system to track which lessons or modules I have marked as complete within a course, so that I have a simple indication of my learning progress.
requirements.rationale: Spk 0's user story 4 captures marking completion, and Spk 1 agrees with the simple progress indication.

requirements.text: As a learner, I want the step-by-step path through a course to be clear, so that I know what to study next without having to figure out the sequence.
requirements.rationale: The user stated they want a clear, step-by-step path so they don't have to figure out what to study next.

requirements.text: The platform shall provide a simple interface focused on learning data science, so that learners are not distracted by administrative or instructor features.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly states they are not concerned about administrators or instructors and just wants a simple place to focus on learning data science.

requirements.text: As a learner, I want courses to be organized by topic (e.g., Python, statistics, machine learning), so that I can easily find courses relevant to my area of interest.
requirements.rationale: The interviewer explicitly asks about grouping by topics as a possible organization method, and the learner's silence or lack of rejection in subsequent chunks suggests this need remains unaddressed by the current user stories.
